extracted.intended_audience: journalists, media activists, the general public, and potential donors
extracted.subtask_description: FAIR's organizational mission and guiding principles for critiquing and improving mainstream media practices, advocating for press diversity and anti‑censorship, working with journalists and activists, and communicating via publications and radio. Describes desired reforms (ownership, public broadcasting, non‑profit media) and modes of public engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advocate for greater diversity in the press
rubrics_metrics.description: FAIR works to invigorate the First Amendment by advocating for greater diversity in the press.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FAIR's mission places diversity of viewpoints as a primary evaluative goal for media institutions and coverage; diversity is pursued through critique, advocacy, and suggested structural reforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scrutinize media practices that marginalize public interest and dissenting viewpoints
rubrics_metrics.description: We work ... by scrutinizing media practices that marginalize public interest, minority and dissenting viewpoints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FAIR performs well-documented criticism of media bias and censorship, focusing on practices that exclude or distort issues important to the public or to marginalized groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-censorship: expose neglected news stories and defend muzzled journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: As an anti-censorship organization, we expose neglected news stories and defend working journalists when they are muzzled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Action includes documenting omissions, publicizing underreported stories, and intervening or advocating on behalf of reporters who face censorship or gagging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote structural reform of media ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: FAIR believes that structural reform is ultimately needed to break up the dominant media conglomerates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizational critique goes beyond individual stories to systemic remedies: advocating policy and structural changes to reduce concentration of media power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish independent public broadcasting
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of FAIR's recommended structural reforms is creating or strengthening public broadcasting institutions that are independent from concentrated corporate ownership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote strong non-profit sources of information
rubrics_metrics.description: Promote strong non-profit sources of information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FAIR supports and encourages non-profit journalism as an alternative to commercial conglomerates and as a means to increase diversity and public-interest reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work with both activists and journalists; provide constructive critique and praise
rubrics_metrics.description: Uniquely, FAIR works with both activists and journalists. We maintain a regular dialogue with reporters ... providing constructive critiques when called for and applauding exceptional, hard-hitting journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation and engagement should be collaborative: offer measured, constructive criticism to reporters while also recognizing and amplifying strong reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage public media activism rather than passive consumption
rubrics_metrics.description: We also encourage the public to contact media with their concerns, to become media activists rather than passive consumers of news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FAIR sees public participation (contacts, letters, activism) as a key metric of a healthy media ecosystem and promotes tools (Action Alerts, email lists) to mobilize readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish and broadcast accessible media criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: FAIR publishes Extra!, the newsletter of media criticism, and produces the weekly radio program CounterSpin, the show that brings you the news behind the headlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multiple platforms (newsletter, radio, email distribution) to document, explain, and publicize critiques; 'news behind the headlines' is a stylistic/content aim for these productions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustain independence through donor support and legal/financial transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Fairness & Accuracy In Reporting, Inc. (FAIR) is a registered 501(c)(3) non-profit organization ... Donations to FAIR are tax-deductible. FAIR’s work is sustained by our generous contributors, who allow us to remain independent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizational independence is framed as a quality criterion: rely on contributor support and transparent non-profit status to avoid corporate influence.
